advice: Experiment: for the approved one-level n=512 Strassen path, replace three separate 256×256 FP32 workspace allocations with one 768 KiB allocation split into left, right, and product buffers. Keep the seven products, FP32 operations, and recombination unchanged. Free the block before gemm returns; on allocation failure, use the existing correct fallback. This is a distinct, unmeasured Strassen wrapper change. Hypothesis: one allocation and free may reduce per-call allocator overhead. Do not clear the workspaces: write both operands fully before each helper call, and rely on the beta-zero helper to overwrite the full product buffer.
risks: Allocator overhead may be small relative to packing and seven subproducts; the larger single allocation may fail where smaller allocations would succeed. Validate fresh inputs, input preservation, full output overwrite and guards, tolerance 0.002 including cancellation and scale-separated cases, allocation-failure fallback, and general sizes and tails. Then use the fixed ten-run paired-control and held-out gates. No speedup is measured or established.
